GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  MEETING MINUTES
  OCTOBER 15, 2019

  1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBER PRESENT:  Schmitz, Zuckerman, Addleman, Carrese, Corman,
  Seamans, Shinn, Silvano, Stegura

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Arata, Bayer, Buresh, Carman, Friedman, Medawar,

  STUDENT MEMBERS PRESENT:  Michael Scandaliato

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Shane Burkhardt, Project Manager, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  Approval of General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes, September 17, 2019

  COMMITTEE MEMBER ADDLEMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 17, 2019.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON AGENDA

  NONE

  5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  VISION AND GUIDING PRINCIPLES

  Shane Burkhardt thanked GPAC members for completing the survey and led a discussion on changes
  to the draft Vision Statement and Guiding Principles, which are as follows:

  Vision (Draft)

  Rolling Hills Estates in 2040 has maintained its rural feel and equestrian identity while becoming a
  more vibrant and connected community. The commercial district is an attractive and thriving
  destination for residents and for visitors from throughout the Palos Verdes Peninsula, providing ample
  opportunities for shopping, outdoor dining, entertainment, as well as living. Rolling Hills Estates is a
  model for sustainable practices, and is admired for its quality local environment, natural setting, and
  recreational amenities, including trails, parks, and open spaces. Residents and visitors can
  conveniently walk, ride horses, bike, and take transit to and within the community. Rolling Hills Estates
  is a family, youth, and senior-friendly city, with safe places for people of all ages to gather, play, and
  learn.

  Guiding Principles (Draft)

  1.  Preserve the community’s distinctive rural character and high quality of life.

  The General Plan maintains and improves Rolling Hills Estates’ quality of life by preserving and
  enhancing the distinctive qualities of existing neighborhoods and the natural environment. The
  General Plan encourages new development with similarly desirable qualities: attractive, safe,
  welcoming, community-oriented. Context-sensitive development ensures built-out rural
  neighborhoods remain rural in character while places with more developable land, such as the

   commercial district, can welcome new residents. Existing and new neighborhoods are supported by
  outstanding public schools, parks, open spaces, community gathering spaces, and well-connected,
  safe, and pleasant streets.

  2.  Improve mobility and emphasize a diversity of transportation choices.

  The General Plan incorporates the development of “complete streets,” which aim to improve
  connectivity, accessibility, and safety for all modes of transportation. The General Plan promotes
  development patterns and enhancements to the circulation network that encourage walking, bicycling,
  equestrian use, and explore the use of transit in order to minimize traffic congestion and reduce
  greenhouse gas emissions. Visible crosswalks, sidewalk bulbouts, stoplights/signs, and signal timing
  ensure safe pedestrian crossings of busy thoroughfares. Sidewalks are traversable for people of all
  ages and abilities, and can easily accommodate strollers and wheelchairs. The City periodically
  evaluates parking standards to respond to changes in parking demand, particularly those associated
  with technological changes.

  3.  Promote an active mixed-use commercial district.

  The General Plan promotes a rich array of activities and uses in the commercial district, including
  neighborhood- and region-serving retail, housing, offices, dining, hotels, entertainment, and other
  compatible uses to foster a walkable mixed-use district. The commercial district has something for
  everyone; new commercial and entertainment uses attract visitors of all ages—including youth,
  seniors, and families—and are closely aligned with local consumer preferences. New and retrofitted
  office buildings provide flexible work spaces. A central community gathering space is the hub of the
  commercial district, and is programmed with public events and activities. Smaller public gathering
  spaces distributed throughout the commercial district give residents the opportunity to relax, play, and
  connect with others.

  4.  Maintain equestrian character.

  The General Plan maintains Rolling Hills Estates’ identity as an equestrian community. Equestrians
  are able to safely navigate and recreate throughout the city via well-maintained equestrian facilities
  and trails. Equestrian identity is reinforced by urban design features throughout the community,
  including signs, three-railed fences, and street furniture. The City provides guidance for homeowners
  who wish to preserve distinctive architectural features of equestrian-style homes.

  5.  Provide quality parks, trails, open spaces, and community facilities.

  The General Plan ensures residents have access to public parks, trails, and open spaces. Parks are
  redesigned as community priorities and demographics change. Public parks provide opportunities for
  active recreation, passive recreation, and equestrian. Community amenities—such as playgrounds,
  skate parks, community centers, fountains, splash pads, and amphitheaters—serve as gathering
  places for youth and families from across the city. Open spaces are preserved for public enjoyment
  and education. The General Plan promotes creating new and expanding existing parks and open
  spaces as opportunities arise. Community facilities provide ample space for community gatherings
  and meetings.

  6.  Enhance the public realm and promote quality design.

  The General Plan cultivates a cohesive image for Rolling Hills Estates with consistent streetscapes,
  well-maintained landscaping, and high-quality building design. New parks, plazas, and gathering
  spaces are designed to be attractive and inviting. The General Plan encourages design diversity and
  visual richness by promoting context-sensitive architectural building styles, responding to a site’s
  topographical constraints, and focusing on sustainability and flexibility to accommodate a range of
  uses and changes over time.

  7.  Become a more sustainable city and protect residents from hazards.

  The General Plan reduces greenhouse gas emissions from energy use and transportation by
  promoting green building techniques, renewable energy, and energy efficiency in new construction
  and retrofit of existing buildings. The City will decrease its reliance on automobiles through increasing
  access to public and active transportation, and infrastructure improvements to promote walking, biking,
  ride-sharing, and zero emissions vehicles. The City promotes land use patterns that minimize
  exposure to hazards including excessive noise, fire, and landslides.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that the second sentence of the draft Vision
  Statement be changed to, “….providing ample opportunities for shopping, outdoor dining,
  entertainment, and living”. The GPAC members agreed.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN suggested that within the third sentence of the draft Vision
  Statement, “natural setting”, should be changed to, “natural semi-rural setting”. The GPAC members
  agreed.

GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
MINUTES, OCTOBER 15, 2019
   In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER SEAMAN, Mr. Burkhardt stated that the Vision
  and Guiding Principles serves as a guide to where the General Plan will be heading.

  The COMMITTEE was in agreement with the Vision and Guiding Principles being the overarching
  theme of the GPU process.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN inquired about the order of the Guiding Principles. Mr. Burkhardt
  responded that the order can be changed if needed.

  The committee participated in a brief exercise to determine their agreement or disagreement with the
  draft Guiding Principles. The GPAC held a discussion and the following changes were agreed upon:

  • Guiding Principle #1 –“The General Plan encourages new development...” change to, “The
  General Plan considers development with similarly desirable qualities…”
  • Guiding Principle #2 – “Improve mobility and emphasize a diversity of transportation choices”
  to “Improve mobility and emphasize a spectrum of transportation choices”.
  • Guiding Principle #4 – No changes.
  • Guiding Principle #5 – No changes.
  • Guiding Principle #6 – On hold for future discussion.
  • Guiding Principle #7 – “Promote an active mixed-use commercial district” to “Promote a vibrant
  commercial district”.
  Taken out of order
  • Guiding Principle #3 – “Become a more sustainable city and protect residents from hazards”
  to “Become a more sustainable city”.

  B.  NOISE AND CONSERVATION

  NOISE ELEMENT

  Mr. Burkhardt provided background on the requirement and provided information on the need for cities
  to include a Noise Element. The major contributor to noise is traffic. He provided the committee with a
  Noise Contour Map, which shows the major arterials and collectors of healthy and unhealthy noise. In
  addition, examples of how changes to building standards could help reduce indoor ambient noise.

  Mr. Burkhardt noted that the current General Plan includes a Noise Element with a threshold as
  recommended by the Governor’s Office of Planning and Research; these recommendations have not
  changed. He further explained the Noise Contour Map.

  Mr. Burkhardt went through the Current Plan Survey Summary and reviewed each policy with the
  Committee. After a brief discussion, the following policies were removed:

  •  Policy 1.4: Require all proposed or remodeled pool equipment to be enclosed in structures
  with sound dampening doors.

  The policy was removed since pool equipment is now quieter and the municipal code has
  setback requirements in place for equipment location.

  •  Policy 1.5: The City will respond to noise complaints associated with household equipment in
  a timely manner.
  •  Policy 1.6: Respond in a timely manner on noise complaints.

  These policies were removed since noise complaints are addressed in the municipal code.

  6.  STAFF ITEMS

  NONE

  7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the committee for their time with completing the survey.

  8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 8:30 p.m. The next General Plan Advisory Committee
  Meeting will be held on Tuesday, November 19, 2019 at 6:30 p.m.
